title: WILD-Diffusion: A WDRO Inspired Training Method for Diffusion Models under Limited Data
claim: With limited data, models show U-shaped validation error and earlier overfitting even though training loss keeps falling, revealing overfitting.
layout: 3 panels in a row; two FID curves, then loss curves; shared x-axis
description: Three line plots side by side, all with x-axis 'Number of images shown to model (M)' from 0 to 200. Panels (a) and (b) plot FID against training progress for FFHQ and CelebA-HQ at 64x64. Each has four colored lines with markers for 10%, 20%, 50% and 100% of the data: gray squares, red circles, blue triangles and green inverted triangles. Smaller datasets reach their FID minimum early, then rise in a U shape and end with higher FID. The 10% curve climbs highest. The 100% curve stays low. Panel (c) plots training loss for all eight dataset and fraction combinations. They are overlapping thin lines that drop sharply and then flatten near 0.1. Legends sit in the upper-left corners. Captions (a), (b) and (c) are below the panels.
caption: Evidence of overfitting in diffusion models with limited data. (a, b) FID curves of DDPM on FFHQ (64×64) and CelebA-HQ (64×64) datasets, both exhibiting a “U-shaped” trend where smaller datasets yield earlier turning points and higher final FID. Percentages (e.g., 50%) indicate the fraction of training data used. (c) Training loss decreases monotonically across all cases.
abstract: Diffusion models have recently emerged as a powerful class of generative models and have achieved state-of-the-art performance in various image synthesis tasks. However, training diffusion models generally requires large amounts of data and suffer from overfitting when the dataset size is limited. To address these limitations, we propose a novel method called WILD-Diffusion, which is inspired by Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Optimization (WDRO), an important and elegant mathematical formulation from robust optimization area. Specifically, WILD-Diffusion utilizes WDRO to iteratively generate new training samples within a Wasserstein distance based uncertainty set centered at the limited data data distribution. This carefully designed method can progressively augment the training set throughout the training process and effectively overcome the obstacles caused by the limited data issue. Moreover, we establish the convergence guarantee for our algorithm even though the mixture of diffusion process and WDRO brings significant challenges to our analysis in theory. Finally, we conduct a set of experiments to verify the effectiveness of our proposed method. With WILD-Diffusion, we can achieve more than a $10$% reduction in FID using only $20$% of the training data across different datasets. Moreover, our method can attain state-of-the-art FID with as few as $100$ images, both in pretrained and non-pretrained settings.
